name: Guided democracy
summary: Guided democracy keeps democratic forms and the language of consensus while placing real direction in a leader and appointed bodies, on the claim that competitive party politics and Western liberal democracy do not suit the nation. In its canonical Indonesian form under Sukarno it combined a strong presidency, a political role for the army, a state-directed economy, anti-colonial nationalism and a Nasakom coalition of nationalists, religious groups and communists.
scope: Profiles Sukarno's Demokrasi Terpimpin in Indonesia (1957-1966): the Presidential Conception of 1957, the 1959 return to the 1945 constitution and the Manipol-USDEK doctrine. Other regimes called guided or managed democracy (Ayub Khan's Pakistan, Pilsudski's Poland, Putin's Russia) are not separately profiled, and answers on topics the sources never discuss are inferred and marked low confidence.

sources.title: Indonesia: Guided Democracy
sources.author: Library of Congress Country Studies (mirrored at countrystudies.us)
sources.usedFor: Army expansion, banning of Masyumi and PSI, functional-group seats, PKI position and seizure of Dutch firms.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Indonesian socialism under Manipol-USDEK stressed social justice and state responsibility for the people's welfare, so state-provided care fits, though the sources never discuss health policy.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Sukarno's regime prioritised national unity and a state-run guided economy over wage policy; no documented stance, and runaway inflation made nominal wage rises moot.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Sukarno attacked "free fight liberalism" and built a Guided Economy with state direction and seizure of Dutch firms, rejecting market allocation as the organising principle.

public-ownership.rationale: Dutch enterprises (shipping, Shell, plantations) were nationalised in 1957-58 and run by the state and army, and Guided Economy was one of the five Manipol-USDEK pillars.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Indonesian socialism and the anti-capitalist, social-justice rhetoric imply burdening the rich, but the documented fiscal practice was seizure and inflation rather than tax policy.

unions-good.rationale: Unions were mobilised through the PKI-linked SOBSI and pushed nationalisation, and the regime valued mass organisations, but under Guided Democracy they were folded into state-controlled structures.

property-fundamental.rationale: Foreign property was seized by decree and the 1945 constitution subordinates private economic interest to the state's social purposes, so property was readily overridden.

regulate-corporations.rationale: The Guided Economy put business under state direction, with Dutch firms taken over and armed forces officers installed to run them.

cut-welfare.rationale: The regime's socialist social-justice framing opposes cutting welfare, though welfare provision was minimal in practice and the sources say little on it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Indonesian socialism favoured state and cooperative gotong-royong ownership rather than worker-owned firms; seized firms went to the state and army, not the workers.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A martial-law regime with reduced civil liberties and an army security role would accept surveillance; nothing is documented on terrorism specifically.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Nothing documented; a state-led moral-nationalist regime that condemned Western decadence would not liberalise drugs.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Never addressed; the regime restricted criticism broadly for national unity, but hate speech as such was not its concern.

strong-leader.rationale: Sukarno explicitly called for a democracy "having a leadership", with the president guiding decisions, and the 1945 constitution gave him broad powers; a strong leader above gridlock is the core idea.

state-harmful.rationale: Guided Democracy was a state-centred system with a state-focused democracy and guided economy; the idea that the state is harmful is the opposite of its doctrine.

limit-guns.rationale: A regime fearing regional rebellions (PRRI, Permesta) under martial law would want weapons monopolised by the state, though no gun policy is documented.

empower-police-military.rationale: The army and police gained appointed seats, ran nationalised firms and expanded their role after martial law in 1957, and Sukarno relied on them to crush rebellions.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not documented; Sukarno's regime launched moral campaigns against Western cultural influence, so legalisation is unlikely though he personally was not puritanical.

decide-locally.rationale: The regime centralised power in Jakarta and crushed the regional PRRI-Permesta rebellions, while appealing to village-style consensus only as a legitimising model.

rehabilitation.rationale: No documented penal philosophy; the regime's use of detention for political opponents offers no clear answer.

traditional-family.rationale: Appeals to Indonesian identity and tradition (the 'Personality' of USDEK) imply support for traditional family life, but the sources never address it.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Not documented, but a nationalist regime built on religious-cultural Indonesian personality, with Islamic parties as a constituency, would firmly oppose it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the religious-nationalist moral climate of Nasakom Indonesia.

more-religion-public.rationale: Nasakom sought to blend nationalism, religion and communism, giving religion a recognised place but banning the Islamist Masyumi; adherents did not push a larger public religious role.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not a Guided Democracy concern; the regime ran anti-Chinese measures yet also anti-colonial rhetoric about historic injustice, so no clear answer.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Never addressed by the sources; no position can be inferred with confidence.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Indonesian Personality was one of the five Manipol-USDEK principles, and Sukarno said Western liberal democracy did not suit Indonesian character.

gradual-change.rationale: Sukarno framed the regime as continuing the revolution (the "rediscovery of our revolution"), rejecting incremental respect for the parliamentary institutions of the 1950s.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Immigration was not an issue; the regime's anti-Chinese measures concerned resident citizens and traders rather than inflows.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Indonesia withdrew from the UN in 1965 over Malaysia's seat and promoted alternative bodies, showing distrust of Western-dominated international organisations.

free-trade.rationale: The Guided Economy and the break with Dutch and Western capital imply protection and state control of trade, as do the nationalisations.

nation-first.rationale: Sukarno pursued West New Guinea by force, confronted Malaysia and quit the UN, subordinating global cooperation to Indonesian national claims and anti-imperial solidarity.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: A regime defined by anti-imperialism and sovereignty would reject intervention in other states on human-rights grounds, though it did itself intervene for territorial claims.

open-borders.rationale: Contradicts the nationalist-sovereigntist outlook and territorial focus of the regime; not directly documented.

limit-growth.rationale: Guided Economy and developmentalist nationalism sought national economic strength; environmental limits were not on the agenda.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is anachronistic for 1957-66 Indonesia; a state-directed regime could in principle order drastic action, but no source gives a stance, so it is left neutral.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Not addressed; the regime relied on mass mobilisation and ideology more than technological optimism.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Never addressed; inferred neutral since prestige-driven modernisation might favour it but nothing is documented.

revolution-justified.rationale: The regime presented itself as continuing the national revolution, but it also repressed rebellions (PRRI) and sought stability, so approval is limited to anti-colonial revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: Sukarno set up a "Cabinet of Experts" and a National Council of functional groups, but the leader, not technocrats, decided and he disclaimed economic expertise.

central-planning.rationale: The Guided Economy implied state-directed development with a five-year plan under Djuanda in 1958, though implementation was patchy and not a full Soviet-style plan.

socialized-markets.rationale: Indonesian socialism was not specified at this level, and the regime did not articulate a position on markets under social ownership.

land-value-tax.rationale: Sukarno's Indonesian socialism never addressed tax design; land reform was discussed but a single land tax was not, so no lean can be inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the socialist social-justice framing of Manipol-USDEK, which would not defend large inherited wealth, though inheritance tax is not documented.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; a regime with minimal state capacity and no tradition of cash transfers would not adopt it.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Guided Economy and nationalisation imply protection of national industry, but the sources do not discuss tariffs.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Guided Economy meant the state steering the economy, with state and army-run enterprises and a state development plan.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Sukarno's socialism opposed large capitalist holdings but also relied on state control; nothing specific on small owners.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Indonesian socialism was not a stateless-communist programme; the regime ran a money economy and wage system even while including the PKI in Nasakom.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: State control of the economy and financial instruments such as the 1959 currency devaluation show the opposite of a market-money view.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: The National Council and functional groups (workers, peasants, military, religious bodies) represented in appointed bodies amount to state-recognised bodies, though not a full wage-and-price system.

one-party-rule.rationale: The regime banned some parties (Masyumi, PSI) but kept a multi-ideology Nasakom coalition, with no single ruling party guided by one doctrine.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: An anti-feudal republic led by a president for life; no monarchical claims, though village-elder guidance had a traditionalist flavour.

democracy-best.rationale: Sukarno called the preceding twelve years of party democracy a mistake and held that Western democracy did not suit Indonesia, though he still styled his system a democracy.

direct-votes.rationale: Decisions were to be reached through leader-guided consultation, not votes; Sukarno disparaged the 50-plus-one logic of competing parties.

workers-councils.rationale: Power was placed in the president and appointed bodies including functional groups, not worker councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: The regime fought regional rebellions (PRRI, Permesta) with the army and held the unitary state sacred.

natural-rulers.rationale: The leadership principle and village-elder model of guidance imply that wise leaders are better suited to guide, though presented as consultation rather than natural aristocracy.

political-violence-never.rationale: The regime used force to crush rebellions, seized firms by force and launched military operations (Trikora, Confrontation).

war-builds-character.rationale: Sukarno's mass mobilisation campaigns and permanent revolution rhetoric valorised struggle, though a direct statement is not in the sources.

separate-church-state.rationale: Nasakom incorporated religion into the state ideology and Pancasila's belief in God, so strict separation was not held, although Islamic-state aims were also rejected.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Sukarno opposed Islamic-state demands and banned Masyumi; religious law was not the basis of the Guided Democracy state.

private-courts-defense.rationale: A state-centred, military-heavy regime would reject private provision of courts and defence.

military-superiority.rationale: The regime built up the armed forces with Soviet arms for Trikora and Confrontation, but 'superiority over rivals' was not articulated.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Indonesia's national doctrine was multi-ethnic (Pancasila, Nasakom unity across communities), though anti-Chinese measures existed.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Nasakom included Marxist ideas, but Sukarno's doctrine stressed national unity, not class conflict as the driver of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Indonesian socialism rhetorically stressed social justice but no documented aim of equal outcomes.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; the nationalist state claimed authority over all land.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Anti-colonial grievance was central (seizure of Dutch firms, NEFO/OLDEFO rhetoric), though reparations are not documented as a demand.

civilizational-union.rationale: Pan-Asian and Afro-Asian solidarity was present, but a religion-based political union was not.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Sukarno demanded citizens put national interest above any group or individual and condemned liberal individualism.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Sukarno said democracy should aim at social justice and not political freedoms, and urged the national interest before individuals.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is absent from the documented doctrine; neutral by indifference.

limit-population.rationale: Sukarno was pronatalist in rhetoric (large nation), but no documented policy; neutral.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Developmentalist nationalism wanted industrialisation; the claim is contrary to its aims though not discussed.

accelerate-technology.rationale: A regime stressing guided order, stability and national unity would not favour disruptive change to institutions; inferred, not documented.

human-enhancement.rationale: Anachronistic for the period; the sources give nothing to infer from.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Inconsistent with leader-guided human deliberation; anachronistic.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A regime with martial law and curbs on criticism would not accept government-proof communications.

restore-past-order.rationale: Sukarno's rhetoric was about revolutionary renewal and building a new order, though he claimed continuity with village tradition and the 1945 constitution.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The regime was heavily ideological (Manipol-USDEK indoctrination), prizing doctrine over pragmatic results.

direct-action.rationale: The regime mobilised mass campaigns but ran elections-and-assemblies in appointed form; mixed.

means-match-ends.rationale: Sukarno's guided system used authoritarian means (martial law, bans) toward a communal consensus goal, so a means-ends match was not its principle.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Guided Democracy aimed at national development, industrial plans and state-run enterprises, the opposite of a return to hunter-gathering.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Not a communist-utopian programme; functional groups presupposed divisions of labour.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Socialist rhetoric about social justice, but no documented endorsement of distribution by need.

production-for-use.rationale: Indonesian socialism opposed capitalist profit-seeking in principle, but sources do not state it directly.

profit-exploitation.rationale: PKI allies held this view, but Sukarno's national-unity doctrine did not endorse a class-exploitation theory.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Nasakom accommodated the PKI but the regime was led by the president and army with no working-class dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: Land reform was talked about, but collective farming was not state policy.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Sukarno's anti-imperialist rhetoric linked imperialism to capitalist powers, but exact theory is not in the sources.

taxation-theft.rationale: The statist regime depended on state extraction and seizure and rejects libertarian views.

harm-principle.rationale: Sukarno rejected political freedoms and criticism as a priority; the state could restrict far beyond preventing harm.

individual-rights-only.rationale: The doctrine put the nation and community above individual freedoms and rejected liberal individualism.

conscription.rationale: A mobilised nation under martial law and war campaigns would accept conscription, though it is not directly documented.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The regime stressed rootedness in the nation; the claim is a libertarian one it would reject.

state-as-business.rationale: The state was a revolutionary and social-justice instrument, not a commercial one.

positive-liberty.rationale: Sukarno said democracy should aim at social justice rather than just formal freedoms, which parallels positive freedom, though not phrased so.

media-academia-power.rationale: Press was brought under state control as "tools of the revolution", so this claim of independent media power would not be a regime concern.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Not documented; the multi-ethnic Indonesian nation and anti-colonial ideology would oppose racial hierarchy claims.

organic-representation.rationale: Sukarno's National Council and legislature seated appointed "functional groups" (workers, peasants, military, religious bodies) in place of competing parties.

total-state.rationale: The regime sought to direct politics, economy and culture through Manipol-USDEK and the Guided Economy, but remained far from total control.

national-rebirth.rationale: The Rediscovery of Our Revolution speech and the claim of returning to the 1945 revolutionary constitution frame the regime as national renewal.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Indonesia seized West New Guinea in 1962 and confronted Malaysia, pursuing expansion of Indonesian reach.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Village-elder guidance echoes it, but formal oaths between lords and followers were not part of the system.

bound-labor.rationale: Contrary to an anti-feudal, revolutionary agrarian programme (land reform demands).

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Manipol-USDEK was imposed as official doctrine, which cuts one way, while Pancasila claimed universal grounds, so nothing decisive can be inferred.

universal-morality.rationale: Sukarno claimed Indonesian particularity rather than universal moral reason; Pancasila contains universal elements.

single-common-good.rationale: Sukarno argued for consensus under guidance toward national interest rather than competing parties bargaining.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Indonesia under Sukarno refused ties with Israel and excluded it from Asian Games, but a statement on the right is not sourced.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return was not an issue for the regime, which instead expelled some Dutch nationals and pressured Chinese traders.

revive-national-language.rationale: Bahasa Indonesia was already the national language; revival not relevant.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Management of seized enterprises fell to army officers and state, not worker or public votes.

school-vouchers.rationale: State-led nationalism opposes privatised schooling choice; not documented.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: The regime financed spending by printing money, with inflation near 100 percent a year.

economic-freedom.rationale: Sukarno rejected "free fight liberalism" and claimed political freedom is not what democracy should pursue.

rule-by-example.rationale: The guidance of a wise leader and village elders were the model; laws and bans were also heavily used.

national-self-determination.rationale: Anti-colonial nationalism was foundational; Indonesia's claims on West New Guinea and opposition to Malaysia were framed as ending colonial domination.

force-without-un.rationale: Indonesia took West New Guinea by Operation Trikora and confronted Malaysia, and quit the UN in 1965.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Nasakom folded religion into the state ideology alongside nationalism and communism, so a reason-only epistemology was not held.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: No welfare state of significance existed and immigrants were not an issue, so the question had no purchase.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Never discussed; welfare conditionality was irrelevant to a mobilisation regime with minimal benefits.

class-collaboration.rationale: Sukarno's doctrine of gotong royong and Nasakom unified nationalists, religious groups and communists in one front, with all groups cooperating for the nation.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Indonesian Personality, one of the five Manipol-USDEK pillars, valorised national heritage; sacrificing it for novelty contradicts that pillar.

dominated-front.rationale: Sukarno's later foreign policy (NEFO versus OLDEFO, Afro-Asian solidarity, break with the West) promoted a front of newly emerging states against Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalist-socialist synthesis; Nasakom organised workers inside a national front.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: The sources record nothing on gender law under Sukarno; adherents' social attitudes ranged between traditional and revolutionary.

ban-interest.rationale: Islamic parties wanted such rules, but the Guided Economy ran on state credit and money creation, so a ban was not adopted.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Contradicts the anti-colonial, multi-ethnic outlook; Sukarno condemned colonial racial hierarchy.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist framing present via PKI, but Sukarno's view of the state was as a national-unifying leader, not a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Army-run Permina took over oil after 1957, showing a development emphasis on domestic oil; no explicit stance.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Immigration was not salient; assimilation pressure on Chinese Indonesians existed but is not part of the doctrine.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiracy of this kind is anachronistic and absent from the sources.

proportional-representation.rationale: Sukarno scrapped the elected parliament for an appointed one, with 154 of 238 seats for functional groups.

national-mission.rationale: Sukarno promoted Pancasila for the world and exporting the revolution to other new states, but a mission to spread a form of government is not clearly documented.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Nothing in the sources on the regime's view of sex-based advantage; no inference is reliable.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Sukarno blamed party politics and its leaders for factionalism, and presented himself as the people's voice against them.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics has no place in the documented doctrine, and the anti-colonial humanist rhetoric points against it.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: The army was central to regime power and was not held accountable for abuses.

night-watchman-state.rationale: A state-directed Guided Economy and Guided Democracy flatly contradict a minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: No documented stance; contrary to the multi-ethnic anti-colonial nation.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Anti-colonial egalitarian claims are present, but regime restricted rights of enemies and Chinese Indonesians.

socialism-one-country.rationale: Indonesian socialism was nationalist and pursued national construction, not dependent on foreign revolution.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Anti-colonial doctrine suggests it, though specific cases are not documented.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: The regime centralised law under the 1945 constitution and rejected separate Islamic law claims, which leans toward one civil law; not directly documented.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Pancasila guaranteed belief in God without ranking faiths; conversion law was not a Guided Democracy issue.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Muslim-majority state with no Hindu-style cattle doctrine would not ban slaughter; inferred from context.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Pancasila's belief in God was incorporated in education; not strongly documented.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Sukarno's regime claimed to be under imperialist encirclement and strengthened state power accordingly.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Sukarno claimed consensus-based village democracy, but denied that competitive elections were the way to get consent.

trade-surplus.rationale: Trade balance doctrine is not documented; the regime's trade policy was politically driven by confrontation with the Dutch and Malaysia.

population-transfer.rationale: Anti-Chinese measures and expulsion of 46,000 Dutch nationals occurred, but not a doctrine on minorities.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The regime launched Trikora, Confrontation and seizures; absolute non-aggression is contrary to it.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Gotong royong and rejection of free-fight liberalism contrast with competition as the engine.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Masyumi and PSI were banned in 1960 for rebellion and opposition to Sukarno.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not a doctrine concern; regime concentrated discretionary power in the president.

separated-powers.rationale: The 1945 constitution concentrated power in the president and the legislature was dissolved and replaced by appointees.

vanguard-party.rationale: The PKI claimed vanguard status but Sukarno's Nasakom was a coalition of currents under presidential guidance, not a disciplined revolutionary party leading the working class.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Social-justice rhetoric under Manipol; the 'wong cilik' appeal.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Council housing is a British issue with no counterpart in the sources.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Martial law restricted strikes in practice, while mobilised unions were co-opted.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Sukarno blamed colonialism and imperialism rather than demography.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Pancasila and Nasakom were built on claiming unity across diverse religious and political currents, which implies diversity need not weaken cohesion.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices were filled by presidential appointment and functional-group selection, with Sukarno holding that leadership should guide, which excludes lots.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The system began under martial law proclaimed in March 1957, with reduced civil liberties against internal rebels.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: A Guided Economy with state direction of trade would permit price fixing; the sources describe inflation but not price decrees, so inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: Newspapers became "tools of the revolution" with criticism curtailed.

party-commands-army.rationale: The army was relatively independent, led by Nasution, and Sukarno balanced it against the PKI rather than controlling it through a party.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Naturalisation rules are not discussed in the sources.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of appointed legislators is not documented.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Party discipline is not discussed; parties were being curtailed in favour of functional groups.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Withdrawal from the UN and confrontation with Malaysia show defence of sovereignty.

head-commands-forces.rationale: The 1945 constitution restored by Sukarno made the president head of government with command of the armed forces and appointment of ministers.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is irrelevant to the doctrine.

clerical-rule.rationale: Sukarno rejected Islamist demands for an Islamic state, banned the Islamic party Masyumi in 1960, and placed authority in the president.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: A nationalist regime mobilising for Trikora and Confrontation expected citizens to support their government in conflict.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: The regime curbed Western cultural influences and kept press and arts as revolutionary tools.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Sukarno was named president for life in 1963, removing any term limit.

recall-officials.rationale: Authority flowed downward from the president, not recall by voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: The regime rejected Western bases and alliances, but did later align with Moscow and Beijing.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing tenure is not documented, and a state-led economy with no home-ownership programme would not impose it.

people-in-arms.rationale: The regime had an army with a strong role plus popular mobilisation, mixed.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The village-consensus model was held up as authentically Indonesian.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: Reclaiming West New Guinea was framed as completing the unity of the former Dutch East Indies.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The regime relied on student and intellectual nationalism as well as populist appeals; neutral by split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Indonesian Personality and anti-colonial claims suggest rejecting hierarchy of civilisations.

death-penalty.rationale: Executions were used against rebels; not a documented doctrine.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Moral campaigns against Western cultural influence suggest scepticism, though curriculum is not documented.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Evolution and creation teaching are not discussed; no inference is possible.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Moral campaigns against Western cultural decadence suggest it.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Citizenship disputes over Chinese Indonesians existed, but no clear regime doctrine.

minority-language-support.rationale: Unity via national language was emphasised; no regional language support documented.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Not documented; Nasakom recognised religion but demanded unity under a common law.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Sukarno demanded putting national interest above any group or individual and curtailed criticism, which opposes encouraging nonconformity.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The regime repudiated Dutch claims and was anti-West financially, though not documented as a general debt policy.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Seizing Dutch assets and building a Guided Economy reflected the view that independence required economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Sukarno dissolved the elected Constitutional Assembly in 1959 and imposed the 1945 constitution by decree.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Sukarno said democracy should focus on state and social justice, not political freedoms; the sources do not link it to growth strictly.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Sukarno accepted aid from both blocs while denouncing dependence, so adherents were split between demanding it and refusing it.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Not documented in this period; no inference possible.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Sukarno was made life president and the head of state was not chosen by direct election during the system.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The state financed deficits by money creation under the president's direction.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Insistence on West New Guinea is of this type, but peace-for-land trades are not documented.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Indonesian socialism and the economic clauses of the 1945 constitution subordinate property to social function, as seizures show.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Sukarno moved closer to Moscow and Beijing, so would not call the USSR state-capitalist.

collective-defense.rationale: Rejected Western alliances like SEATO but not collective defence in principle.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The regime viewed Dutch retention of West New Guinea as illegitimate colonial occupation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Banning Masyumi and rejecting Islamic state demands put political religion under state authority.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Sukarno, as president, was an active political leader guiding national direction, not a symbolic head above politics.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: The army crushed the PRRI and Permesta regional rebellions, and Sukarno's martial law of 1957 was a response to secessionist unrest.

region-keeps-system.rationale: The regime centralised power in Jakarta and treated regional autonomy demands as rebellion.

sacred-ruler.rationale: A leader cult developed around Sukarno, who was named life president, but neither the sources nor his doctrine claim divine descent.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Flat tax conflicts with socialist redistributive framing; inferred, not documented.

character-from-environment.rationale: Socialist and revolutionary-renewal view of changing people; not documented.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Sukarno ruled by decree and broad presidential powers and replaced the legislature.

space-expansion.rationale: Not a priority for a state struggling with inflation; anachronistic.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Not discussed; the 1945 constitution blended presidential power with an assembly, but no theory of mixed rule was stated.

leader-cult.rationale: Sukarno became life president, with his speeches as state doctrine (Manipol-USDEK) and mass praise.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law was not a Guided Democracy concern and the sources give no basis for a lean, so neutral.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Nasakom stressed cooperation among classes and currents, so continued class struggle was not its view.

land-redistribution.rationale: PKI support came from land reform demands and the regime pursued land reform laws, although the regime avoided confronting landowners.

refugee-return.rationale: The doctrine never addressed refugee return, and the regime's own expulsion of Dutch nationals cuts neither way for descendants' return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Greater-Indonesia claims on Malaysia partly rested on kin peoples (Maphilindo), but the sources record these as anti-neocolonial.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Pancasila's belief in God without a state religion and Nasakom pluralism point against criminalising apostasy.

women-must-cover.rationale: Islamist dress mandates were not adopted, and the regime opposed Islamist-state demands.

common-currency.rationale: The regime asserted national monetary control, as the 1959 devaluation shows; shared currencies are not discussed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Sukarno floated a Malay-world union (Maphilindo) briefly, but also fought Malaysia, so adherents were split.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: The doctrine was of a unitary nation under one ideology, not autonomous minority institutions.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: The statement concerns persecuted minorities abroad, which the doctrine did not address.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: PKI-aligned Nasakom members held this, while Sukarno stressed ideas, will and national spirit, so the regime was split.

ban-cartels.rationale: Competition policy is not documented; the state directed the economy instead of promoting competition.

no-bailouts.rationale: The state routinely took over and directed firms, so refusing support to failing enterprises was not its approach.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Sukarno saw checks as impeding national will, though he did not say it about courts.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The break with the Dutch and the West and Guided Economy had autarkic tendencies, but not a closed colonial bloc.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Anachronistic; trade-linked standards were not discussed.

moral-incentives.rationale: Revolutionary mobilisation rhetoric used moral appeals, but not a stated programme.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: The regime itself suppressed armed rebels, and the PKI then followed a parliamentary and front strategy.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Anti-feudal republican nationalism, though local aristocrats persisted.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Indonesian Personality (a Manipol-USDEK pillar) implies teaching national history centrally; curriculum is not documented.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Anti-colonial doctrine, with Dutch rule in West New Guinea attacked as colonialism.

patriotic-education.rationale: Manipol-USDEK was taught as compulsory indoctrination and the Indonesian Personality stressed national pride.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Racial preference policy in admissions and hiring is outside the documented doctrine; the regime's anti-Chinese trade measures do not settle it.

public-money-creation.rationale: The state financed spending by money creation, but no theory is documented.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Manipol held that capitalist imperialism was in decline and had to be opposed, which sits badly with expecting it to adapt.

former-empire-influence.rationale: The statement concerns former imperial powers; the doctrine was anti-colonial and did not address this.

delink-world-market.rationale: The break with Western capital and NEFO ideology had delinking features, though Indonesia still sought aid.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: A statist anti-colonial regime stressed national unity and state direction, contradicting a libertarian freedom to discriminate.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: The 1945 constitution was returned to for presidential powers, not rights protection.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Indonesia rejected the Dutch settlement and the Round Table agreements; the regime wrote off colonial arrangements.

elective-rulers.rationale: Sukarno disparaged competitive elections, yet the presidency was legitimised through the MPRS.

minority-veto.rationale: Musyawarah-mufakat seeks consensus but the leader guided and overrode dissent in practice, as bans on parties show.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Opposition to Sukarno was handled as rebellion, with Masyumi banned and the PRRI crushed, so a right of resistance was denied.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Sukarno dissolved the legislature in 1960 and replaced it with appointed bodies.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Not discussed; the regime's rhetoric was populist rather than paternalist.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The regime demanded mass mobilisation and putting the national interest above private concerns.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Not discussed; the regime itself used mass media as tools of the revolution.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: A Gramscian claim not in the sources.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Neocolonialism rhetoric (NEFO) held rich Western powers exploited new nations.

native-born-offices.rationale: Anti-Chinese measures and nationalism hint at it; not documented.

party-own-road.rationale: Sukarno's own Indonesian socialism was a nationally distinct path; PKI accommodated.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The regime launched "stand on our own feet" (berdikari) rhetoric late, though aid was taken in practice.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Insistence on West New Guinea (taken in 1962) illustrates it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Not relevant to a post-colonial majority-indigenous state.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Not documented; the 1945 constitution predates this European debate.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: The regime included communists in Nasakom and opposed anti-communist framing.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: A US historical question with no counterpart in the sources.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monument controversies are not documented for the period; the regime built its own national monuments but left no stated view on condemned figures.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources contain nothing on gendered disadvantage in education or health, so no position can be inferred.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Domestic violence policy is not discussed in the sources on Sukarno's system, so neutral by absence.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Sukarno argued Western liberal democracy did not suit Indonesian character and proposed village-based guided democracy instead.

military-guardian-role.rationale: The army gained appointed seats and a security and economic role, and the 1957 martial law created that role.

paid-care-work.rationale: Recognition of unpaid domestic labour is not part of Manipol-USDEK or any documented regime policy.

filial-duty.rationale: Sukarno appealed to village traditions of consensus under elders, which suggests respect for seniority; filial duty itself is not documented.

office-by-exam.rationale: Posts were filled by presidential appointment and political balance, though Sukarno also installed a Cabinet of Experts.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Dutch firms were seized and foreign companies excluded in a Guided Economy.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Divorce law is not discussed in the sources; religiously grounded family law was left largely to the religious courts, so no lean.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The president could dissolve bodies; delegates were not recallable.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: A state-directed economy would not hand pensions to private companies; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The statement echoes socialist land policy, but the regime's land reform stayed modest and unclear.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament was dissolved in 1960 and replaced with appointed assembly.

single-official-language.rationale: Bahasa Indonesia as national unifier; the sources do not document restriction of others.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Seizure of Dutch assets and economic nationalism suggest barring foreign land ownership; no explicit rule is documented.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The disparate-impact standard is a modern legal doctrine absent from the period and its sources.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The regime campaigned against Western consumer culture and imposed austerity rhetoric; not documented as a position.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Sukarno backed infiltration into Malaysia; Confrontation included guerrilla incursions.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: The regime opposed outside powers meddling in new states, such as US aid to the PRRI rebels, though it sent forces beyond its borders itself.

corporate-influence.rationale: Anti-capitalist, anti-Dutch-business stance implies concern about corporate power over politics.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Seizure of foreign firms and anti-Western stance support it.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: No documented population policy or family incentives under Guided Democracy, so neutral.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local limits on property purchase are not documented; the regime's property focus was on seizing foreign assets.

job-guarantee.rationale: Social-justice rhetoric suggests sympathy, but no jobs policy is documented.

democratic-peace.rationale: Sukarno rejected Western-style democracy as unsuited to Indonesia and would not make its spread a project for peace.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Sukarno demanded citizens subordinate themselves to the national interest under guidance, which denies a right to disregard law.

non-intervention.rationale: Sovereignty and anti-imperialism imply non-intervention, though Indonesia itself used force against Malaysia and in New Guinea.

industrial-unions.rationale: Not documented; unions were organised through SOBSI along mixed lines.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Not part of the doctrine, though anti-Chinese measures existed.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: No such programme exists in the doctrine, which stressed traditional Indonesian identity.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Newspapers were made tools of the revolution and criticism was curtailed, so a right of access was not recognised.

local-production.rationale: Not documented; Guided Economy stressed national self-reliance, not local production.

informal-organisation.rationale: Mass organisations were centralised under the National Front.

national-law-over-international.rationale: The regime defied the UN and held its sovereignty above outside bodies.

religious-nation.rationale: Pancasila and Nasakom define the nation as religiously plural.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: The regime's anti-imperialism, NEFO-OLDEFO view and breaks with the Dutch and the UN reject tributary deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Centralisation of revenue and fights against regional rebellions over resource control.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Indonesian socialism did not set out a theory separating personal belongings from means of production, so no clear answer.

defeat-communism.rationale: Sukarno allied with the PKI in Nasakom and shifted towards Moscow and Beijing.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: State-led economy; no documented support for independent providers.

religion-illusion.rationale: Nasakom kept religion as a pillar; the regime rejected atheism as official ideology.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Anti-capitalist socialist outlook; some national-bourgeois role acknowledged.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Sukarno wrote on women's role in the revolution, but the sources opened here do not tie sex equality to economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare is not documented as an aim of the Guided Economy.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Language policy under the regime concerned promoting Indonesian as the national language, not purging foreign words, and the sources are silent on it.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaty relations with internal nations are not discussed; the regime treated regional autonomy claims as rebellion, which leaves no clear lean.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Gotong royong village imagery inspired the doctrine, though no programme of cooperative communities was carried out.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Sukarno's Nasakom combined with communism; the third-way element was Indonesian socialism, but included communists.

historical-land-claim.rationale: West New Guinea claim based on inheriting the Dutch East Indies.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not documented; the claim is not part of the doctrine.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Not documented; criminal law was not a focus.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Masyumi and PSI were banned, critics curbed and the press made a tool of the revolution.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Blasphemy law is not discussed in the sources, and Nasakom's religious pluralism gives no clear direction.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: The regime was founded on anti-colonialism and took West New Guinea from the Dutch, rejecting rule for a metropole's benefit.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Not part of Sukarno's doctrine; Muslim parties differed.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: The regime fought Islamist rebellions and banned Masyumi, rejecting removal of rulers for not governing by religious law.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Citizens participating through functional groups guided by leaders, not direct popular decisions.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: This analytical framework is anachronistic for the period and absent from the sources.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Not documented; the cultural climate was socially conservative.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not documented; religiously informed ethics suggest opposition.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Nasakom sought to combine nationalism, religion and communism into one front.

alienated-labor.rationale: Marxist-influenced PKI allies held it, but Sukarno's doctrine did not state it.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Indonesia is Muslim-majority and the regime included Islamic parties in Nasakom.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Pancasila includes belief in God but authority came from the revolution and the leader.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Official dress rules for religion are not documented for the regime, so neutral.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Workplace harassment procedures are an anachronistic concern with no basis in the sources.

social-market-economy.rationale: Guided Economy meant state direction, not a market economy with social protection and fair-competition rules.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: The army gained a central political and economic role under Guided Democracy and was used to take West New Guinea.

rich-first.rationale: Egalitarian socialist rhetoric and state-directed economy oppose letting some get rich first.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Non-aligned posture of Afro-Asian leadership, though tilting toward Moscow and Beijing.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The regime made Sukarno president for life, but no dynastic succession was planned.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual banking is not part of the documented Guided Economy, which relied on state credit and money creation.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Sukarno broke with Western finance and the Dutch and denounced neocolonial dependence, so he would reject outside austerity terms.

property-franchise.rationale: The regime relied on mass mobilisation and populism, not a propertied electorate.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Ecofeminist thought is anachronistic and absent from the regime's doctrine.

reification.rationale: A Marxist-humanist concept not stated in the sources on Sukarno's doctrine, so neutral.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Sukarno said free speech mainly benefits the upper classes and ordinary people do not use it, which parallels this claim.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Sukarno restored the 1945 constitution by presidential decree and ruled with decrees and martial-law powers.

racial-franchise.rationale: A multi-ethnic anti-colonial nation did not restrict suffrage by race.

online-participation.rationale: Internet participation is anachronistic for 1957-66 and the sources offer nothing to infer from.

open-government-data.rationale: The press was controlled and criticism curtailed, so open publication of decision records was against the practice.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not documented; Indonesia later restricted it but the Sukarno-era doctrine did not address it.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not documented, though anti-Chinese trading measures existed in 1959-60.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Guided Democracy placed direction in the president and appointed functional-group bodies, not in lot-chosen citizens, so assemblies that help decide are inferred as unwelcome; the sources never discuss sortition.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Inferred from Sukarno's modernist, nationalist approach, which sought to reconcile religion with a modern state in the Nasakom formula; the sources do not address doctrinal reinterpretation.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Sukarno condemned free-fight liberal capitalism and wanted a state-directed economy; inferred, since the sources do not address wealth and liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Inferred from the nationalist-traditionalist, army-backed order of Guided Democracy; the sources do not discuss military service.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Guided Democracy rested on Pancasila with belief in God and a Nasakom coalition including religious groups, so state promotion of atheism was not its position.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: A strong presidency and a political role for the army imply keeping coercive state institutions; inferred, not discussed in the sources.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Nasakom set out a guaranteed place for nationalist, religious and communist blocs in government rather than majority rule by parties.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: A state-directed economy and mass mobilisation under the leader imply the state, not charity, leads social provision; inferred.

term-limits.rationale: Sukarno's leader-centred system aimed at lasting direction rather than rotation of officeholders; inferred, as the sources do not discuss term limits.

vote-delegation.rationale: The system replaced competitive voting with direction by a leader and appointed bodies, so citizen-controlled delegation runs against it; inferred.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The regime never addressed existential risk and nothing in its principles settles it.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist and Islamic-majority setting; the sources do not discuss religious office.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The sources do not address marital authority, and nothing in the doctrine settles it.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Sukarno's system put national interest above group claims and an appointed, leader-guided politics; inferred that extending the vote to non-citizens would not fit, though the sources never discuss it.

rent-control.rationale: Inferred from the state-directed economy and Indonesian socialism of Manipol-USDEK, which favoured state control over market outcomes; housing is not discussed.

abolish-ip.rationale: Inferred from the anti-Western, nationalist economic stance, which would not favour abolishing protections that foreign-linked industries use; intellectual property is not discussed.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from the regime's mobilisation of the population behind national campaigns and the army's expanded political role; youth movements specifically are not covered in the sources.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Inferred from Sukarno's anti-colonial, non-aligned nationalism, which resisted great-power military presence; nuclear basing is not discussed.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Guided Democracy was anti-imperialist and anti-neocolonial, and the sources describe confrontation with Western powers and seizure of Dutch assets, so foreign bases on Indonesian soil would be rejected.

recognise-genocide.rationale: The sources do not discuss genocide recognition, and the regime's own 1965-66 aftermath makes the position unclear; left neutral.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the socialist element of Manipol-USDEK and its state-directed economy, which favoured rewarding labour over property ownership.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Inferred from the central role the regime gave the army and national defence; a pacifist rejection of self-defence is far from its doctrine.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Sukarno's nationalism appealed to an Indonesian identity rooted in pre-colonial history, which fits continuity claims, but the sources do not spell this out.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not a concern of the doctrine; inferred that a nationalist, statist regime would treat sex as given and not socially constructed.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the regime's collective, national framing of politics over identity-based critiques of categories.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from nationalist honouring of independence-struggle heroes, which the regime used for legitimacy; the sources do not discuss martyr language.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Sukarno's Nasakom combined nationalists, religious groups and communists in a pragmatic coalition, so politics as a good-versus-evil spiritual battle fits it poorly.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Indonesian nationalism aimed to gather the nation in one state; a homeland serving as a cultural centre for a diaspora is not part of the doctrine and is inferred away.

culture-before-state.rationale: Guided Democracy prioritised state-building and political reorganisation under strong leadership, so cultural renewal first is inferred to be contrary to it.

god-not-male.rationale: Pancasila belief in one God is part of the state ideology, but the sources say nothing about gendered descriptions of God; left neutral.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Inferred; the regime had no feminist theology and would be unlikely to judge religious texts on this test.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from the economic nationalism of the period and the seizure of Dutch firms, with pribumi preference as a common aim; the sources do not state it for minorities.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Guided Democracy defended the unitary state against regional revolts and federalism; merging regions by people is inferred to cut against that.

independent-unions.rationale: Under Guided Democracy unions were folded into state-controlled structures and mass organisations served the leader's line, so independence from the state was not a principle; inferred from that practice.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Nasakom put communists and the army in a leader-directed framework and Sukarno rejected class-struggle politics in favour of national unity; the regime never made worker power a test of socialism (inferred).

local-essentials-public.rationale: The Guided Economy put key enterprises under state control; local utilities were not discussed, so this is inferred from the statist economic line.

second-chamber.rationale: The legislature was an appointed body including functional-group representatives and the 1945 constitution's consultative assembly; a true second chamber balancing an elected parliament ran against concentrated direction (inferred).

municipal-property.rationale: Property was nationalised to the national state and army, not to local communities; the system centralised direction in the president.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Guided Democracy centralised authority in the president and Jakarta and rejected local deliberative decision-making as a route for politics, so confederal local assemblies do not fit.

family-wage.rationale: The sources never discuss family wages; the regime's welfare rhetoric is not specific enough to take a side.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Drug regulation was not discussed and the regime's economic crisis left health policy marginal; no stance can be inferred.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Anti-ageing research was outside the regime's concerns in 1957-66; no stance can be inferred.

anonymous-payments.rationale: A regime directing the economy, banning parties and seizing foreign firms would not accept untraceable money beyond state control; inferred from its control orientation.

online-anonymity.rationale: The regime curbed the press and banned parties and its leader's line demanded conformity, so protecting anonymous participation is unlikely; inferred from that practice.

person-over-state.rationale: Sukarno put national interest above individuals and groups and rejected liberal individualism, so the person is not held above the state's ends.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Manipol-USDEK and Nasakom brought religious groups into the coalition and the 1945 constitution rests on belief in one God, but the regime was also dominated by secular nationalists and communists; adherents are split.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Guided Democracy centralised power under the 1945 constitution and the president, so regional self-government existed only at the centre's discretion; inferred from the unitary line after the 1957-58 regional rebellions.

gm-crops.rationale: Agricultural biotechnology was not discussed and predates the regime's concerns; no stance can be inferred.

dense-cities.rationale: Urban form was not an issue for the regime; no stance can be inferred.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Sukarno's doctrine put the nation's interest above groups and Nasakom joined religious and ideological streams, so organising by racial group is outside its nationalism.

racial-pride.rationale: Sukarno's anti-colonial nationalism stressed national, not racial, pride, though it rejected colonial racial hierarchy; inferred and not clearly about race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: The regime pursued confrontation with Malaysia and the seizure of West Irian, so it did use force beyond pure defence; adherents justified these as anti-colonial struggle.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Sukarno's nationalism bound many language groups under Indonesian unity and also claimed wider Malay lands, so language was not the stated test; the sources do not address it.

communal-electorates.rationale: The system placed political groups under national guidance and functional groups, with Nasakom a state-managed coalition rather than separate communal voting; inferred.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Manipol-USDEK was built as a campaign against Western neocolonialism and imperialism, and the regime treated outside powers as threats to the nation.

free-public-college.rationale: Indonesian-style socialism stressed state responsibility for the people's welfare, which fits free public education; the sources do not state it.

pollution-taxes.rationale: A state-directed economy under presidential guidance favoured direct control and mobilisation over market pricing of pollution; inferred.

future-generations.rationale: Sukarno cast his regime as completing a revolution for later generations, but the sources never discuss environmental duties; inferred.

women-distinct-values.rationale: The sources show no stance on women's distinct values; the regime's mass organisations included women but made no such claim.

arms-reduction.rationale: The army expanded and the regime pursued confrontation with Malaysia, so arms reduction ran against its practice.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Sukarno's foreign policy was assertive and anti-Western, and the sources show no commitment to open treaty-making; inferred.

capital-controls.rationale: The regime seized Dutch firms and ran a state-directed economy that put national interest over free capital movement.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The army was expanded and given a political role; Sukarno also backed civilian armed volunteers, so adherents were not strict, and this is inferred.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Sukarno's regime relied on the army and anti-colonial confrontation; inferred that soldiers refusing to fight would be rejected.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Labour was organised into functional groups under state-led Nasakom politics, not free bargaining; inferred.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Anachronistic tax-system device the regime never discussed; the state-directed economy used other tools, so this is neutral.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from a state-directed economy that gave leaders discretion over spending, not legal limits on borrowing.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Guided Democracy was anti-colonial and anti-imperialist and pursued confrontation with Western economic powers, including seizing Dutch firms (s4).

smash-state-machine.rationale: Sukarno used the existing bureaucracy and army, returning to the 1945 constitution by decree, and did not dismantle the state.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Manipol-USDEK set a state-directed 'Indonesian socialism' as the official line, not open economic experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Never addressed; inferred from a state-directed economy aimed at national development.

sacred-nation.rationale: Nationalism and national unity above groups were central to Manipol-USDEK, though the 'sacred' wording is inferred.

student-debt-relief.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the stress on social justice and state responsibility for welfare.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Inferred that Jakarta's regime stressed national unity and put down outer-island regional rebellions, rather than treating regions as colonies.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Pancasila includes a just and civilised humanity, which implies common human dignity; inferred.

public-service-media.rationale: Party bans and controls on the press show the regime would not keep media independent of government; inferred.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Inferred from Sukarno's Nasakom synthesis and the Indonesian state's belief in God, which treated religions as compatible parts of one nation.

farm-price-support.rationale: Inferred from the state-directed, anti-capitalist 'Indonesian socialism' of the Guided Democracy economy.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Inferred from anti-colonial strongman nationalism that prized strength against rival powers; not stated in the sources.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: Guided Democracy sought a unified national front and functional groups led from above, rather than independent class parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Inferred from a modernising, centralising state that overrode local custom; the sources do not discuss it.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from Sukarno's modernist nationalism, which favoured national law over adat; not stated in the sources.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Inferred from the unifying national-language policy of Indonesian nationalism, which made one Bahasa Indonesia over regional names.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred from state-directed economic management; private-suit-only regulation does not fit.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Inferred: the regime centralised authority in the president and functional groups, with no formal place for customary chiefs.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Inferred from the developmentalist, state-first priorities of the regime; environmental limits were not an issue.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, leader-directed approach to order that limits judicial independence.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the nation-building emphasis on a unified national culture and language.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Sukarno's regime channelled labour into state-aligned functional groups and Nasakom organisations; a right-to-work stance is not documented, so this is a neutral inference.

voter-id.rationale: The sources do not discuss voter identification; under Guided Democracy elections were postponed and the question had little practical meaning.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Nasakom sought to balance nationalist, religious and communist currents and Pancasila gave no creed legal precedence, though this is inferred, not stated in the sources.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Guided Democracy rejected competitive party elections as alien to Indonesia and placed direction in the leader and appointed bodies, so a purely electoral test of democracy is denied.

premarital-sex.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the conservative social norms of the Indonesian state, though Sukarno was personally unconventional.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Anachronistic; inferred from the regime's martial-law controls on press and communications to maintain order under the 1957 emergency.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Inferred from a state-directed economy under Indonesian socialism that favoured state programmes over market-style cash transfers; not discussed in the sources.

women-suffrage.rationale: Women voted in Indonesia's 1955 elections and the regime did not revoke the right, but the sources do not address this directly.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The Nasakom coalition included religious groups, so the regime did not frame religion as oppressive; inferred, not stated in the sources.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; anti-colonial nationalism stressed national unity over race theory, so no stance is documented.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not documented in the sources; the regime had mass women's organisations such as Gerwani but no clear policy on dedicated state agencies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Sukarno's state-directed economy and socialist rhetoric make first-claim ownership unlikely; inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Sukarno's anti-colonial nationalism put sovereignty first and distrusted Western institutions; inferred.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Nasakom joined nationalists, religious groups and communists under Pancasila, so no single scripture was privileged; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; no clear stand.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Its economy was state-directed, so a planned state would plausibly be defended; inferred, not stated.

indirect-election.rationale: Guided democracy placed direction in appointed bodies and consensus, not competitive direct election.

national-church-status.rationale: Pancasila and Nasakom gave religions a shared place and did not set up a state church; inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: The regime stressed a unitary state under the 1945 constitution and the army put down regional rebellions; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Indonesia claimed Dutch New Guinea on colonial-border grounds rather than through a local vote; inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Indonesia claimed the whole of the former Dutch East Indies; inferred from that claim.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are not documented either way.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Unitary nationalism favours settlement anywhere in the state; inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no clear stand.

missingStatements.text: Political decisions should be reached by consensus under the guidance of a leader or elders rather than by majority vote.
missingStatements.rationale: Sukarno's case for Guided Democracy rested on adapting village-style deliberation and consensus under guidance in place of party competition and majority rule.
missingStatements.declined: Consensus-under-elders is a narrow variant of rejecting majority rule; minority-veto and rule-by-example already separate it, and the audit answers minority-veto -1, so merging would conflict.

notes: This audit rests on secondary accounts plus one primary diplomatic record of Sukarno's speech, since his own speeches (Presidential Conception, Rediscovery of Our Revolution) could not be opened in full text. Most answers on issues the regime never addressed (gender, bioethics, climate) are low-confidence inferences. Other guided or managed democracies (Pakistan, Russia) would differ on the economy, religion and the left.
